title: The Sale-Sign Trick
intro: Shops spend millions on signs. Today you learn to read them like an analyst.

blocks.html:
Remember the dinner-table puzzle?

Shop A: a top for £50 with 10% off.
Shop B: the same top for £45, no discount.

Time to settle it with numbers.

blocks.prompt: Work out what you actually pay in Shop A.
blocks.hint: 10% of £50 is £5. Take it off the price.

parts.label: So which shop is cheaper? (A, B, or same)

blocks.button: So why does the sign work? ✨
blocks.html:
Both shops charge £45. But the 10% OFF sign makes Shop A feel cheaper — your brain sees a bargain before it does any maths.

Shops know most customers never check. You always will. That's the analyst's edge.

blocks.prompt:
Two coats, both marked £100.
Shop A: 30% off.
Shop B: £25 off.
blocks.hint: Shop A: 30% of £100 is £30 off. Compare what you pay in each.

blocks.html:
Now the other classic sign: “WAS £80 — NOW £60”.

Analysts always ask: what percentage off is that, really?

Money off: £80 − £60 = £20.
As a fraction of the old price: 20 out of 80 = a quarter.
So it's a 25% discount. Now you can check any sign in any shop.

blocks.prompt: ★ A jacket's sign says: WAS £120 — NOW £90. What percentage off is that?
blocks.hint: Money off first: £120 − £90 = £30. What fraction of £120 is £30?

blocks.prompt: ★ Sneaky one. A game says WAS £50 — NOW £40. The shop claims “25% OFF!”. Is the sign telling the truth?
blocks.hint: £10 off. What fraction of £50 is £10? Compare with what the sign claims.

blocks.html:
📈 Your first field assignment, analyst: this week, find one real sale sign — a shop window, a website, anywhere. Write down the WAS and NOW prices, work out the true percentage off, and report to the board at dinner:

1. What did the sign want you to feel?
2. What was the real discount?
3. Verdict: honest sign, or trick?

done.title: UNIT 1 COMPLETE 🍋✓
done.html:
The Percentage Toolkit is yours: 10%, 5%, 1%, 20%, 25%, 50%, 75%, combinations — and now the analyst's move: working out the percentage from the prices, which is how you catch a shop bending the truth. Three weeks ago you told me percentages were your struggle. Look at you now.
